title: Version manifest (<kind>s/<name>/<version>.json)
description: The machine-checkable form of m053 section 6.3 -- the only document that decides what gets installed. The root validates shape alone; a validator selects #/$defs/submitted or #/$defs/published, because entry_signature can only be produced by the registry and so is forbidden on a submission and required once published (section 6.7). Rules that span two documents -- the owner match against repository, index-matches-manifests, immutability across a diff -- cannot be expressed here and live in the validator.

kind.description: Must match the directory this manifest was read from.

name.description: Kebab-case identifier, unique within the kind.

version.description: Exact semver, equal to the filename stem.

accent_version.description: Host range supported, as a semver requirement such as ">=0.24.0". Matched against the crate version with any prerelease suffix removed (section 11.5). The requirement grammar admits comparator lists, tilde/caret operators and wildcards, so no pattern here can settle it: the validator parses it exactly as the client does before any download, and rejects what will not parse.

api_version.description: Plugin WIT generation, as an exact semver version. Plugins only.

trust.description: Provenance and review tier. Never a claim about the code.

distribution.description: registry: fetched from artifact.url. external: delivered out of band by the vendor.

islands.description: Island component names this artifact registers. Island names share one global registry per page, so a plugin should namespace its own (acme-forms:signup).

entry_signature.description: Registry signature over the whole manifest. Written by CI at merge, never by the submitter.

attestation.description: Additive vendor provenance. Never the sole gate.

yanked.description: Retracted: still resolvable by exact pin, never chosen as latest.

allOf.description: A registry entry is fetched from a URL, so it publishes one, its digest, and its transfer size.
An external entry carries no download URL -- that is what makes it external. It may still publish a digest so install --from can verify a hand-delivered file.
api_version is the WIT generation a component was built against. Neither a theme nor a template has one.

submitted.description: A submission: the registry holds the signing key, so the author cannot supply entry_signature and a document carrying one is rejected. Requiring it here would make every third-party PR unmergeable.

published.description: The merged tree: CI has stamped the signature.

artifact.description: Where the bytes are and what they must hash to. The URL is an absolute third-party URL, never relative to the registry base: the hub never serves artifact bytes.

size_bytes.description: The transfer size. A bound on the download, never on what it expands to.

seller.description: vendor: the third party sells directly. accentx: sold through the AccentX store.

price_hint.description: Display only. Never authoritative -- the seller's page is.

allOf.description: A commercial entry must say where to buy and who takes the money; the CLI prints the first when a licence is missing.
